title: VPC Upgrade Conductor: controlled orchestration and rollback scheduler for zero-downtime runtime rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a VPC Upgrade Conductor service and Terraform hook set that coordinates staged runtime rollouts in private deployments with automated health gating and a scheduled rollback scheduler. The conductor's goal is zero visible downtime for tenant traffic: it will perform small incremental shifts, validate behavioral and infrastructure-level health signals, optionally run shadow traffic verification, and trigger automated rollback windows when health quorums fail. This ticket covers design, IaC changes, health probe definitions, canary ramp policy, and a deterministic rollback scheduler that integrates with the existing control plane and customer VPC networks.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can schedule and execute a 5-stage canary rollout across a tenant slice in staging using the new Terraform hooks
Health gating uses at least three independent signal classes (synthetic probes, KV-cache hit-rate, and latency p50/p99) and enforces quorum rules before further ramping
Automated rollback scheduler triggers a rollback without manual intervention when quorum fails for a configurable window and publishes diagnostics to the Console
No increase in 99th percentile request latency for live traffic beyond configured SLO (baseline + 10%) during verified rollouts in staging
All Terraform changes are backward-compatible; customers with pinned modules see predictable plan/apply with no resource replacement unless explicitly requested
implementation_notes: High-level approach: implement a stateless Conductor service that sequences rollout phases and talks to the existing control plane API. Add Terraform lifecycle hooks (null_resource local-exec and module outputs) to create per-rollout ephemeral ACLs and rollout metadata in the customer's VPC state. Health probes: add a synthetic 'probe agent' sidecar that executes representative prompt sets and reports pass/fail plus latency distributions. Define quorum logic: require 2/3 signal classes healthy for two consecutive evaluation windows before increasing traffic. Canary policy: 1%, 5%, 20%, 60%, 100% by default with configurable dwell times. KV cache priming: after each ramp, warm KV entries using sampled requests routed to a priming path; priming must be bounded and observable. Rollback scheduler: when quorum fails, mark rollout as suspended and schedule an automatic rollback after a grace window (default 5 minutes) unless a human overrides in the Console. All Conductor state is emitted to Console events and to an S3-compatible bucket for audit and post-mortem. Terraform changes will be encapsulated in a new module 'redwood_vpc_rollout' exposing settings for canary policy, probe endpoints, and rollback windows.
rollout_plan: Create Terraform module 'redwood_vpc_rollout' with module inputs for canary percentages and probe endpoints
Add probe-agent container and health endpoints to the data-plane Helm chart for private deployments
Implement Conductor service HTTP API: start_rollout, get_status, suspend, resume, abort, force_rollback
Wire Conductor to the control plane and existing routing layer to perform percentage-based traffic shifts
Run end-to-end tests in staging with synthetic customers (3 tenants) using the default canary policy
Observe telemetry for two full cycles; tune quorum thresholds and dwell times based on staging results
Roll out to a small set of production tenants behind feature flag and monitor closely for 48h
rollback_playbook: Automatic: upon quorum failure for two consecutive windows, Conductor marks rollout as 'suspended' and begins a rollback timer (default 5m). If no manual override, Conductor rolls back to previous healthy revision and emits diagnostics to Console.
Manual via Console: operator can 'abort' to immediate rollback or 'suspend' to pause ramps and investigate. Console provides 'diff' of network changes and recent probe failures.
Post-rollback: run a focused verification sweep (synthetic probes + smoke tests) before re-attempting a rollout. Capture trace IDs and attach to incident artifact.
If rollback fails repeatedly for same tenant slice, escalate to 'tenant quarantine' path: pin to last-known-good runtime and open a support ticket with priority P0
metrics_and_alerts: Rollout success rate metric per tenant (goal 99.5% across planned rollouts)
Quorum-failure-rate alert when >1% of rollouts in a day fail health gating
Latency SLO breach alert for affected tenant slices (p99 > baseline + 10%)
KV cache priming failure rate and priming duration percentile dashboards
Conductor error rate and API latency dashboards (SLO 500ms)

notes: Trade-offs considered: tight dwell times reduce customer exposure but increase chance of false positives on transient infra blips. We bias toward slightly longer dwell times plus quorum-based validation to avoid noisy rollbacks. Terraform approach favors additive resources and ephemeral ACLs to avoid forced replacements in customer-managed VPCs. Operational burden: Conductor introduces another control-plane component; mitigations include stateless design, short retention for ephemeral state, and strong automated cleanup after rollback or completion.
